clip1.text: Fraud analysts review alerts one transaction at a time.
But the risky pattern often hides in the connections between accounts and devices.
Rebuilding that picture by hand is slow, and an innocent link is easy to mistake for a suspicious one.
TraceGuard traces those connections and writes an evidence-linked brief with Gemini on Vertex AI.
The graph decides, the AI explains, and every claim is checked before you see it.
Case C-1: four wallets send five transfers into A-07 within thirty minutes, seventeen thousand pesos in total.
Thirty minutes later, A-07 sends fifteen thousand five hundred onward. A payment made before the money arrived isn't counted.

clip2.text: I run the AI investigation: a fixed workflow runs the graph tools, then Gemini explains the results.
Before anything is shown, every citation and every figure is checked against the tool output. This panel shows what was verified.
Both rules flag a pattern that warrants review. The counterevidence comes from the tools: two senders aren't on the shared device, and less went out than came in.
Clicking a citation highlights the exact records on the graph, right beside the brief.
I can ask a follow-up. Who owns A-22? The data can't say, so TraceGuard refuses instead of guessing.

clip3.text: C-2 is three accounts sharing one tablet. No rule matches, so the evidence is insufficient: device sharing alone proves nothing.
In C-3 the money trail reaches the edge of the data at A-22. The next recipient and the intent are stated as unknown.
TraceGuard runs on Cloud Run with Gemini on Vertex AI, least-privilege access and no API keys.
Connected evidence, cited, and honest about what it doesn't know. That's TraceGuard.
